en:
A ragged sash handed down from the previous
generation. It looks tattered enough to tear
any moment, yet it is so tough that it won't
tear easily. Wearing this sash will straighten
you up -- not just your clothes, but your
heart and spirit too.

A blanket with a picture of Impala Banchou on
it. It is said to be a replica of the favorite
blanket of a certain country's queen. Like the
original, it even reproduces the rich aroma.
note: New name: Impala Banchou (inpara banchou, banchou = gang boss), romanized. 'a certain country's queen' = [JP] (probably Ragnastia; not named, so kept vague).

en:
Princess Leafa: "Going off on your next
adventure without a word to me -- what nerve!?
So suddenly! What am I... supposed to... Um...
Are you really... leaving...? ...I see. Very
well. Then take this sword. Even under another
sky, you are my proud Sweet Ginger Knights!"
note: New names: Princess Leafa (riifa; matches the 'Leaf Blade' pun), Sweet Ginger Knights (suwiito jinjaa kishidan). Elminage II farewell-gift text.

en:
A historic costume made for bards with the
finest voices. It bears the 'habits' of the
great bards who wore it, so it guides the
wearer's posture, and they say it lets them
sing as finely as those before. It is also
said to shift through seven colors with the
quality of the voice.

Grand Merchant Walmitt: "Hello in this form,
eh? Keeping well? Gregorio -- I thought him
useless, but he turned out good at splitting
wood. He's at it happily now. With that face.
I'm not the sentimental type, but... take this
hat. Adventure in it, and don't get swindled
by shady merchants! Farewell."
note: Walmitt as in ebt glossary. New name: Gregorio. Compressed to fit: 'You'll adventure in my hat, so don't let a strange merchant fool you' -> 'Adventure in it, and don't get swindled by shady merchants!'.

en:
Jela: "I wanted the boss to say goodbye too,
but the boss went nuts collecting hanafuda.
A-ahaha..." Jelatan: "Jelatan ishn't to blame!
Boss ish a maniac!" "From the two of us,
here's some armor." "Shnacks too!" "I'll
always be praying you're all safe. Come back
sometimes!" "Yesh!"
note: Jela (as in 'Jela's General Store'); New name: Jelatan (jeratan, baby-talk -deshu rendered as a lisp: 'ish', 'Shnacks', 'Yesh!'). The boss (oyakata): gender unknown, so no pronoun. Wording lightly compressed; the unlabelled quotes keep the source order (Jela / Jelatan alternate) with no added speaker tags.

en:
Archbishop Mersenne: "Ngh... HAAAAAAH!! It's
Mersenne! Thanks for helping Namina the other
day. She then passed the cathedral's
ordination exam with flying colors and now
serves at Semnadoc! Now it's our turn to help.
I'm sending you this staff. Feels lucky,
doesn't it? Blessings upon you!!"
note: New names: Archbishop Mersenne, Namina. Semnadoc as in 'Semnadoc Cathedral'. [JP] rendered 'ordination exam'.

en:
An anklet wrapped in fluffy fur given a sleep
effect, made from the pelt of an animal that
died in hibernation. Adds sleep to any bow and
arrow. It also brings its owner sound sleep;
when worn, it seems to pulse faintly,
thump-thump.

A weapon whose pattern works as a magic seal,
adding confusion to its owner's attacks.
Tracing the pattern with a finger or following
it with the eye confuses anyone, owner or not,
so handle it with care.
note: Source calls the anklet a 'weapon' (bow accessory); kept.

en:
A weapon set with a charming jewel. Once the
jewel enters your sight, you cannot help being
charmed by its beauty. These jewels sell for
high prices, but whether that is due to the
charm or to honest appraisal, no one can say.

An anklet that wraps loosed arrows in vacuum
blades, giving them the power to behead. Now
mass-produced, but the first was said to be a
wind spirit in love with an adventurer who
changed form to stay with them forever. The
Beheading Anklet you got... perhaps the one
you hold now is 'the one'.
note: [JP] -> 'vacuum blades' (item [JP] = Vacuum Blade). Adventurer's gender unknown: 'them'.

en:
An anklet that senses magic and makes arrows
fly straight at its source. Made by Yuja, a
witch tormented by past sins and cursed so she
could not take her own life, so that Polyte
would shoot her. Legend says Polyte's
superhuman skill avoided a fatal wound, and
Yuja, persuaded, set off to atone.
note: New name: Yuja (yuuja). Polyte as in glossary.

en:
King Montana: "Looks like I made it in time.
Heard you're off on a new adventure, so I
looked for a parting gift. How's this? Well,
it's the only decent thing I had. Getting Holy
Granny Ubogenya's Pubic Bone would just be
sad, right? It's never been used! Go on, take
the leap! I know you can do it!"
note: New names: King Montana, Granny Ubogenya (ubogeenya-baa). 'Holy Granny Ubogenya's Pubic Bone' is a joke item name, kept at full crudeness.

en:
A sash said to be wearable only by those in
holy orders. The moment it is put on, it peers
into the wearer's heart; if they are unfit, it
slips right off. But if they are fit, it is
said to bind tight and never come loose.

A charm blessed for family safety, success in
studies and such. It is given by parents or
close friends. Its power is uncertain. Still,
it is a real joy to see how much someone cares
for you take shape like this.

A charm given when one must send loved ones
off to a dangerous place. Unlike the everyday
charms handed out lightly, it carries the
giver's earnest prayer for a safe journey.
With it, your hearts will stay joined, however
far apart you are.

This armor exists not as an object, but as a
mass of vibrations. Even deflecting a sword is
really the vibrations holding the blade back.
It has an affinity for water and is always
cloaked in moisture, so it is sometimes
mistaken for water-element armor.

A strangely shaped sword, as if it were
nothing but floating bowstrings. It is said to
come apart into 11 parts, but only divine
wisdom could take it apart, or so they
predict. Its strokes are hard to read, so it
should prove very useful in real combat.

A military uniform only certain ranks may
wear. Perhaps clothes shape the heart: even
the most pathetic soul who puts it on is said
to stand up straight and speak crisply.

Its maker prayed for travelers' safety by the
name carved inside the jewel. But whose name
could it be? If you have it, prayer will give
you strength to face every hardship. Treasure
it until you have truly grown strong. Altouche
does not choose its owner; it will protect
you.

A strange spear worn on the hand. Its tip
spins, letting it attack by boring holes into
the foe's body. It is said to pair well with
magic puppets.
note: [JP] = magic puppet (glossary term).

en:
A lavishly ornamented magic gun. It looks like
a kind of bow, but as it was made by chance,
how it works is hard to grasp. Like a bow it
hits distant foes, and with skill you can even
bounce shots off walls to hit enemies hiding
behind cover.

An absurd weapon born of an accident. Its
blade truly runs on endlessly, but
weaponsmiths scorn it as heresy. Yet its
cutting power is too good to ignore. Picture
your armor slowly being shaved away by this
blade, and you won't sleep at night.

A tiger-striped loincloth. Wearing it, you
feel strength bulging through your muscles. If
you pick a weapon to match, it has to be a
club. Strike a cool, buff pose!

The finest fried rice, cooked fast over high
heat so every grain is separate. One bite
feels like rice dancing in your mouth. As an
item it can be sold to shops, but it will
never be in stock.
It can be sold to shops, but it doesn't keep,
so it will never be in stock.
note: The source itself holds two versions of the last sentence (an old and a revised one, on separate lines); both kept, one row in one row out. Drop the first if the build wants only one.

en:
Shortcake made with lavish amounts of the
finest cream and the strawberries called the
king of strawberries.
As an item it can be sold to shops, but it
will never be in stock.
It can be sold to shops, but it doesn't keep,
so it will never be in stock.
note: Same duplicated last sentence as row 2134; both versions kept.

en:
A scroll-shaped food said to have come from
the eastern lands. You lay vinegared rice and
your choice of fillings on seaweed, roll it up
and eat it. It can be eaten one-handed, so it
is popular with busy people.
note: 'scroll-shaped': the item is in the scroll category.

en:
Gauntlets made with the fur of a legendary
fox. True to the tale of the fox that caught
its prey with nimble moves, wearing them is
said to let you dodge enemy attacks with ease.

A sword adorned with Politan, king of kings of
all beasts. Only a king of kings can wield it,
so its edge and worth are beyond measure. But
said to be worth more than the sword is
Politan itself: catch one alive and the bounty
will keep three generations in idle luxury.

Every maid carries her pride as a maid, and
that pride shows in her headband. This
headband has a certain shine, bringing out its
wearer's presence with modest boldness. Put it
on and you will awaken to your calling as a
maid.
note: Source sentence 2 is garbled ([JP]); read as 'it shines and brings out its wearer's presence'.

en:
A sexy bikini made from turtle shell. Made for
female adventurers who always want to be sexy,
it manages to show off sexiness without giving
up a fair amount of defense. If there is a
female adventurer you like, why not give her
one as a present?

Throwing kunai bearing talismans with great
power against evil spirits. The strong
talismans let them deal damage directly even
to spirit bodies. Ninja are said to always
carry a Geimaga somewhere on them to deal with
spirits.
note: Geimaga as in ITEM slice_16. The source ends on a comma (typo); ended with a period.

en:
Rather flashy for glasses, but there is a
reason. They hold a spell that lets you tell,
looking through them, whether you have seen
something before or are seeing it for the
first time. All this ornament exists for that
spell.

Step right up, folks, if you're in no hurry!
It's everyone's favorite Lucky Bag! What's
inside is a surprise for after you buy! Good
and bad, all packed in together! But that's
the fun of it! So, what's inside? Getting
curious now, huh!! Buy quick before they're
gone! First come, first served!!
** Work in progress **
note: Designer placeholder on the '(Enemy-only below)' separator row; translated literally.

en:
A sticky fluid that many monsters make inside
their bodies. Each monster's is different:
sometimes it is plain liquid, sometimes it is
like a powerful acid that melts whatever it
touches in an instant.

A sleep-inducing mist so thick you can see it.
It stays afloat in the air for a long time, so
it can be packed into leather bags. There is
even a technique for turning the packed mist
into sleeping medicine.

The fangs lining a monster's mouth. Perhaps
the slight curve is a design to keep bitten
flesh from getting away.

The bloodless hand peculiar to the spirits of
the dead. The belief that a hand should be
warm makes it feel all the colder.

A weapon beasts are born with. Most curve like
hooks and are used to scratch and tear. Their
tips can also dig into the ground, letting
beasts run fast, among other things.

A venomous fang. It is somewhat modest in size
next to other fangs, but its sharpness and
killing power are vicious beyond compare. It
bites and punches holes in the skin, then
pumps deadly venom from its tip to weaken the
prey.

A monster's tentacle. They range from slimy
ones to vicious spiked ones. They are a
tentacled monster's hands, and its weapons.

Rocks left untouched by human hands for ages
are said to be spiritually sublimated and to
hold special power. These are the rocks
spirits attack with; the higher the
sublimation, the more freely they can wield
them.

A technique that reacts keenly to the hearts
around it. If a foe feels hostility toward the
user, it projects that hatred back as a
psychic shockwave. The greater the foe's
hatred, the stronger it gets. If you can treat
all things with love, a Psi Blade will never
hit you.

A blow from a tightly clenched fist is simple,
yet deep. From an amateur, a normal punch
might hit harder, but if someone well-built
brings one down on you, be very wary.

Vines from an old tree. Their strength and
power are nothing much, but their long reach
lets them attack foes one-sidedly. We say 'old
tree', but they are part of the monster's own
body, and many reportedly get angry at being
called that.

A weapon monsters are born with, mostly
growing from the head. It is mainly used to
charge and skewer a foe, but it can also meet
your weapon to parry swords and the like.

The claws of the Kin of Darkness. Being
natural, they differ little from us scratching
with our nails. But the foe uses them clearly
as weapons, so do not underestimate them.
note: [JP] = Kin of Darkness (glossary).

en:
Condensed water fired like a bullet. Even mere
water becomes a terrifying weapon given speed
and mass. A powerful monster can easily punch
through plate mail with it.

A stretchy sticky thread, strong and tacky. As
liquid it hardens on contact with air and
grows strong like thread. The goo tingles to
the touch. Not a thread you want to touch, but
soaked in medicine it changes into fine
thread, often used in crafts.
note: No ITEM name yet for [JP] (lit. 'numbing sticky thread'); the description never names it.

en:
A claw far too sharp for an ordinary beast;
one look tells you it is dangerous. Wild
animals live where life and death are always
side by side. Poke at one out of curiosity,
and a weapon like this will beat nature's
rules into your body.

A hand that radiates a dangerous will to draw
you into its kind. Higher spirits are said to
be not just cold: they can steal life force
with a mere touch.
note: [JP] rendered 'you'.

en:
A technique that uses the centrifugal force of
spinning to boost an attack. It says 'wheel',
but there need be no wheel. You may swing a
sword in a circle around yourself, or ram a
foe while spinning.

The scythe of a giant mantis. How many insects
has that blade hunted? You may get it by
defeating its owner, but even a lifeless
scythe must look like a threat to insects.

A tentacle its owner trained on purpose to
attack with, until it evolved into a weapon.
It hits with whip-like force, and at times
even following its motion is hard. Unless you
can react even when you can't read it, assume
you have no chance to win.

A technique that controls the wind, makes a
vacuum vortex in the air and slams it into a
foe. Spirits excel at it, and once you know
the magic principle it is surprisingly easy to
cause. But even then it is hard to control, so
we cannot master it without training.

The rich buy the fangs of large beasts as
ornaments. Some adventurers make a living on
contract with them, cutting the fangs off
their kills to sell.

The claw of a spirit with no body. Being
wounded by a spirit body your attacks can't
even touch is hard to accept.

A vine covered in sharp thorns. It can be used
like a spiked whip. The thorns are meant to
anchor the vine and stick seeds onto birds and
beasts, so once they snag, yanking them out
easily wounds the prey.

A deadly kick unleashed by four-legged beasts.
A bullet-like blow born of wild muscle can
deal fatal damage even to a warrior who takes
it unguarded. This is the power of nature.
note: No ITEM name yet for [JP] (lit. 'fierce hoof').

en:
A fang with stronger venom and bite than a
normal poison fang. It is shaped to slice
wounds open, helping the venom spread. The
truly dangerous ones are said to kill you if
you just snag a finger on the poison fang of a
slain beast.

They open and close slowly, but crustacean
muscle is said to let them cut anything. They
carve bone-in meat with ease; being caught
bare would be deadly. Fight monsters with
these carefully, or you may watch a loved one
torn apart before your eyes, helpless.

A tail with a venomous stinger. Attacking with
a tail is like having an extra hand. That
alone is a nuisance, but it carries poison
too. Even a graze is dangerous, so if your foe
has one, mind your distance.

The claw of a lesser dragon. Lesser, yes, but
still a dragon's claw. It is very sharp, and
its strength is beyond measure. Dragon claws
are often used to make weapons and armor.

A so-called tongue kiss. What effect this
attack has depends on who it's used on. But no
attractive partner would go smooching just
anyone. The only one who would attack like
this is... you-know-who.
note: No ITEM name yet for [JP]. [JP] read as 'the one it is used on'. [JP] (that one) kept gender-neutral as 'you-know-who'.

en:
An arm imbued with fire magic. Some are born
that way; others wrap flames around it with
magic. It is common among fire spirits and the
like, but do not even think of copying it.

A fang that releases a nerve venom. What makes
it scary is that, however bad the odds, a
single bite might turn the tables. If your foe
has one, be very careful.

The prow of a ghost ship. The old ship's
grudge has hardened at its tip, longing for a
new captain's orders. Weigh anchor! Read the
charts! Hard to starboard!! Now, whoever
stands in our way, with this huge prow we'll
riiiide them dooown~~~ R-A-M T-H-E-M!!
note: No ITEM name yet for [JP] (lit. 'hazy prow'). [JP] (run them over and kill) -> 'R-A-M T-H-E-M'; the spaced-out spelling keeps the chant.

en:
A fang that sucks out life force. For the Kin
of Night, it is a kind of refinement. Power is
not the point; the 'act' of sucking life force
holds special meaning for them. They also love
to enslave their prey, and many seem to fall
under their spell.
note: [JP] 'Kin of Night', patterned on glossary 'Kin of Darkness'.

en:
Fangs of mighty beasts are also used as
ornaments and tools of sorcery. Unlike our
weapons, a beast kills to live. So the power
of beast fangs is held sacred, and many seek
to share in it.

The hard beak of a bird. It depends on the
kind, but a truly hard one can even bore out
wood.

Made of strange ice that never melts. The
sword itself is very fine, high-grade even
among monsters' weapons. If you equip it,
bring gloves: the bitter cold could give your
hands frostbite.

Both bow and arrows are silver. A loosed arrow
pierces its target trailing glittering silver
motes. Its accuracy is said to vary greatly
with its owner's skill.

Originally a sword drawn in a painting. When
the painting took on magic and began moving
freely, the sword took form along with it. Now
it can be swung like any ordinary sword.
Strange, isn't it?

The claws of a fiend beast painted on a
canvas, given form along with the beast. Rumor
says their power depends on how good the
painting is.
note: [JP] 'fiend beast', as in ITEM name 'Fiend Beast Claw'.

en:
The claws of beasts that are no ordinary
animals, but have gained the power of
darkness. Made more savage, these fearsome
claws, built for pure destruction, overwhelm
adventurers.

An ogre's broadblade. Clumsy-looking, but the
perfect shape for smashing with brute force.
The grip is wound round and round with
non-slip cloth. Grip: excellent.
note: [JP] kept as the English 'excellent' joke.

en:
One move derived from the fist is the
Umeboshi, from the eastern lands. You make
fists with both hands and grind them into both
of the foe's temples. It works wonders on
kids.
note: [JP] (umeboshi, the temple-grinding noogie) romanized as the move's name.

en:
A finger shining as if divine. Its owner feels
nothing, but to anyone else it is searing hot.
Its normal attacks are strong, but it is
vicious enough to turn a foe to stone just by
pointing at them.

Ordinary tentacles move vaguely, pushed by
shifting body fluids, but this one is driven
by real muscle. Think it's the same as before,
and a supple, lashing arm will slap you.
